PLAN 13 | SHOTS 13A–13D | POSSESSION — CORRECTED EYE INSERTS

Create a 15-second cinematic sequence for Seedance 2.5.
Horizontal 16:9.
Four shots lasting four, four, three and four seconds.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
Zahhak and his living shoulder serpents = {{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}
Shahrnaz = {{CHAR_SHAHRNAZ}}
Arnavaz = {{CHAR_ARNAVAZ}}

PROP REFERENCE:
Serpent-headed staff = {{PROP_STAFF}}

Preserve the exact referenced identities, costumes and mask designs.

MASK CONSTRUCTION AND MOTION:

Each woman wears a rigid sculptural mask with existing eye openings. Her real eyeballs are visible behind those openings.

Treat the mask as a solid, inanimate object firmly secured to her head.

During both eye close-ups, the camera, head and mask remain completely stationary. Every contour, opening, carved eyelid shape and surface detail stays registered in exactly the same screen position.

Animation is confined to the real eyeballs behind the fixed openings.

The blackening effect belongs exclusively to the visible surfaces of the eyeballs. Surrounding skin and mask material retain their original appearance.

LOCATION AND LIGHTING:

The chamber is concealed by complete darkness.

One fixed hard overhead spotlight casts cold-neutral light vertically onto the subjects. Highlights reveal upper mask edges, small portions of the eyes, the staff carving and the hand.

The surrounding image remains black. Architecture and floor remain unexposed.

Keep lighting and exposure constant. Preserve a tiny overhead catchlight on the eyes so their curved surfaces remain readable during the black phase.

SPATIAL STATE:

Shahrnaz stands WEST and Arnavaz EAST, both facing NORTH.
Zahhak stands NORTH of their midpoint, facing SOUTH toward them.

His RIGHT hand holds the staff, its head centered between their sightlines at eye level.

The inserts depict details of one simultaneous possession event.

SHOT 13A | 00:00–00:04 | THE STAFF UNDER TENSION

100mm macro lens, approximately f/2.8, with a narrow plane of sharp focus.

Camera EAST of the staff head, looking WEST. Its carved snout points SCREEN-LEFT toward the sisters.

The rigid carving fills most of the frame. Focus on its nearest ridge and carved eye; the remaining contours soften into darkness.

A minute tremor from Zahhak’s grip travels through the staff. Its shape and material remain unchanged.

Make a slow three-centimeter approach, maintaining focus on the carving.

Power is suggested through tension, vibration and sound.

SHOT 13B | 00:04–00:08 | SHAHRNAZ — BLACK EYES

100mm macro frontal close-up from NORTH of Shahrnaz, looking SOUTH.

Frame both existing eye openings and the bridge of the mask between them. Keep both exposed eyeballs in focus.

The camera is locked off.
Shahrnaz’s head and mask remain motionless.
The eye-opening edges stay identical in shape, size and screen position throughout.

00:04–00:05:
Only her eyeballs rotate upward behind the stationary mask openings.

00:05–00:06:
As they reach the upward position, a uniform black coloration spreads across the visible eyeball surfaces, covering iris and sclera.

Both openings now reveal completely black eyeball surfaces, retaining their curved volume and a tiny reflected overhead highlight.

00:06–00:07:
Hold both eyes fully black. Her head and mask remain perfectly still.

00:07–00:08:
The black coloration recedes. Her original iris color and natural white sclera return as the eyeballs rotate down into their initial position.

End on a calm, fixed natural gaze.

SHOT 13C | 00:08–00:11 | ARNAVAZ’S HAND

85mm close detail of Arnavaz’s empty RIGHT hand beside her right thigh, photographed from slightly NORTH-EAST.

Her fingers curl inward and gather a small fold of her own clothing.

A fine tremor passes through her fingertips and wrist, making the fabric quiver.

Her fingers then release together. The fold drops and her hand hangs loose.

Hold the relaxed hand for the final half-second.

The overhead light defines the hand against black.

SHOT 13D | 00:11–00:15 | ARNAVAZ — BLACK EYES

100mm macro frontal close-up from NORTH of Arnavaz, looking SOUTH.

Frame both existing eye openings and the surrounding mask surface.

The camera, head and rigid mask stay locked in place. Preserve every edge of the openings as a stationary boundary.

00:11–00:12:
Her real eyeballs rotate upward behind the fixed openings.

00:12–00:13:
A uniform black coloration covers the entire visible surface of both eyeballs, including iris and sclera.

00:13–00:14:
Hold the fully black eyes. Tiny overhead catchlights preserve the appearance of solid, curved eyeballs behind the mask.

00:14–00:15:
Restore the original iris color and white sclera while the eyeballs rotate down to their initial position.

End with natural eyes and an unnaturally calm gaze. Her head and mask remain stationary through the final frame.

VISUAL CONTINUITY:

The mask is a fixed physical shell.
Eye rotation and eye coloration occur behind its unchanged openings.
The black phase covers the eyeballs completely, then fully reverses.

Whenever Zahhak’s living serpents enter a frame edge, retain subtle muscular movement and their established single-headed anatomy.

SOUND:

Faint grip tension around the staff.
A caught breath during each upward eye movement.
Soft fabric tension and release during the hand insert.
Slow exhalations as the eyes return to normal.

NO MUSIC, NO DIALOGUE.

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_1>>> is Zahhak (CHR-001 V08); match it wherever Zahhak appears.
<<<image_2>>> is Arnavaz (CHR-004 V01); match it wherever Arnavaz appears.
<<<image_3>>> is Shahrnaz (CHR-005 V01); match it wherever Shahrnaz appears.
<<<image_4>>> is Dagger Horse Head (PRP-019 V02); match it wherever Dagger Horse Head appears.
<<<image_5>>> is Staff - Bronze Cobra (PRP-001 V01); match it wherever Staff - Bronze Cobra appears.
